correctness.rationale: The three-space dichotomy is complete: all-affine subspaces have <=q zeros; any determinant-containing subspace contains two independent affine constraints, whose common solution is empty or an affine plane of size q^2. Equality is equivalent to det being affine on that plane, with a bijection between optimal subcodes and eligible planes. The polarization identity identifies all eligible directions: for q>2 exactly the 2(q+1) rank-one directions; for q=2 exactly 15 symplectic-isotropic directions. Multiplying by q^2 translates gives the stated multiplicities. The finite verifier enumerates all 1395, 33880, and 376805 three-subspaces and independently all eligible directions over fields of size 2,3,4; it returns VERIFY_OK and 60,72,160, consistent with the proof. This does not infer an all-field result from finite testing.

originality.rationale: The fully examined 2019 Piñero–Singh manuscript (Theorem 3.11 and Example 3.13, pages 13–16) gives one-codeword weights and counts for C^A(2,4), not the common-support multiplicities for three-dimensional subcodes; its individual weight enumerator does not determine the three-subspace incidence statistic. Datta–Ghorpade 2015 concerns numerical generalized Hamming weights; Yadav 2026 revisits one-codeword weight spectra, as confirmed by the dated abstracts and available indexed sections. Independent published-record and exact-parameter searches, including algebraic-geometric aliases, revealed no explicitly identical all-prime-power extremizer classification. This is a bounded, non-certifying novelty conclusion: full text of two plausible manuscripts was inaccessible, and an earlier unpublished or unindexed equality-case enumeration remains possible.

value.rationale: The statistic is the exact number and geometric classification of all support-minimizing three-subcodes of a naturally occurring affine Grassmann evaluation code, not a randomly selected finite parameter. Generalized Hamming weights record only the minimum support sizes, while higher-order support multiplicities distinguish the entire extremal incidence structure. The binary field exhibits 60 extremizers instead of the 24 from naive continuation of the two-ruling formula, explained by the difference between quadratic functions and their finite-field linearizations. The theorem covers every prime power and makes a substantive structural distinction; no unsupported generalization to other code levels is claimed.
